findings.title: Data race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` across `errgroup` workers in `init`
findings.body: In `searchSupport.init`, each `group.Go` closure mutates the outer variables `totalBatchesIndexed` (`totalBatchesIndexed++`) and `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) without synchronization. Previously, `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu.Lock()` for the entire build, which largely serialized these workers; with fine-grained locking in `BuildIndex`, multiple workers now execute `s.build` and assign to `err` concurrently whenever `WorkerThreads > 1`. This causes a data race (failing under `-race`) and can cause a worker's `return err` to read another goroutine's `nil` error, silently swallowing index build failures.

findings.title: Concurrent map read in `TotalDocs` and map write in `BuildIndex`
findings.body: `searchSupport.init` starts the background watch goroutine (`s.handleEvent` -> `s.getOrCreateIndex` -> `s.search.BuildIndex`) before calling `s.search.TotalDocs()` on line 216. In `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` (`pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:146`), `b.cache` is iterated without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`, while `BuildIndex` writes to `b.cache` under `b.cacheMu.Lock()`. If a watch event arrives for an unindexed resource while `TotalDocs()` is running, Go will panic with a concurrent map iteration and map write error.

findings.title: Removing `s.Init` checks from RPC handlers makes `Stop` state checks ineffective
findings.body: `server.Stop` sets `s.initErr` to `"service is stopping"` / `"service is stopped"` (lines 321, 328, 339). Previously, every gRPC handler called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returned `s.initErr` once `s.once` had completed, rejecting new requests after `Stop` was called. Because the `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Read`, `List`, `Watch`, `Search`, `History`, `Origin`, `IsHealthy`, `PutBlob`, and `GetBlob`, mutations to `s.initErr` in `Stop` are never read and requests continue to be processed after `Stop`.
